question: Will Spain's registered unemployment fall in September 2026 compared to August 2026?

calls.reasoning: Historically September almost always raises Spain's registered unemployment (declines in only 2 of 18 years since 2008: 2021 and 2025), so the unconditional base rate is ~13%. But the regime has drifted hard: +17.7k (2022), +19.8k (2023), +3.2k (2024), -4,846 (2025). Naive trend continuation implies a modest September 2026 decline. Corroborating: mid-September 2026 Social Security data (17 Sep release) is stronger than the same point in 2025 - +204,392 affiliates 1-15 Sep and +90,097 seasonally adjusted over two fortnights, vs +123,357 and +51,779 in 2025 - with YoY affiliation growth of 3.23% vs ~2.2%; back-to-school hiring is running hot and the August base (2,355,918) is high. Against: August 2026's +44,419 was nearly double August 2025 and far above the ~15.4k consensus, with a POSITIVE seasonally adjusted change (+3,184) despite a smaller-than-usual affiliation loss - a divergence suggesting register inflow (plausibly the April migrant regularization cohort) unexplained by job destruction, which could persist into September and flip the sign. YoY register improvement has also decelerated from -6.0% (Sep 2025) to -2.91% (Aug 2026). Net: expected change roughly -5k with a ~12k SD, so YES is favored but far from safe. No prediction market prices this (none on Polymarket/Manifold/Kalshi; Spain blocked both platforms in May 2026), so no crowd anchor. Low tier, single draw.
calls.reference_class: September month-over-month change in Spain's registered unemployment (paro registrado), 2008-2025 - 18 observations, declines only in 2021 and 2025
